newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech share mkt surges but clouds loom - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Czech share mkt surges but clouds loom - analysts.

text.p: Czech shares surged on Tuesday after a sharp fall in the crown but analysts warned that the euphoria would fade as the reality of high interest rates and poor company fundamentals came back to haunt investors.

The RPIX real time index of key shares closed up 6.2 percent to 1,043.5 led by SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka -- the three most heavily capitalised bourse issues -- which all rose by 8.0 percent.

"There's short term bullish sentiment. The stock market should rise on the (depreciation) news. I think that in the longer term though you have to be more sober and look at the interest rates," said John Vax of ING Barings.

Shortly after the Czech National Bank (CNB) on Monday evening said it would no longer resist pressure for a weaker crown, the CNB hiked the discount rate to 13 percent from 10.5, indicating that it wanted to limit the currency's decline.
On Tuesday, the crown was trading 8.5 percent below Monday levels at around 19.50 to the mark.

Analysts said that despite the obvious attraction of cheaper stock prices to foreign investors, many companies could be severly hit by the rise in the cost of borrowing and, in some cases, the cost of servicing foreign currency debt.

"Definitely, those companies will be hit with foreign exchange loans as well as the companies with higher debt equity ratios because it is expected that interest rates will not go down to the original pre-crisis level," said Miroslav Nosal of Patria Finance.

ING's Vax suggested that the CNB may even have missed an important opportunity on Monday night to devalue the crown and relax its tight monetary policy, which is widely blamed for the country's economic slowdown, at the same time.
"If they'd cut interest rates and devalued the crown a little bit or widened the band then I think (that would have been) good...but they didn't do that."
"For a lot of the economy, it's the high interest rates that (are) killing," he added.
Czech shares have taken a battering from several sides in recent months pushing the official PX50 index down by over 20 percent since hitting a two-year high of 629 in late February.

Apart from high interest rates, investors blame the downturn on poor capital market regulation, a lack of company restructuring, which led to poor first quarter earnings, and most recently the instability in the crown.

Jan Sykora of Wood and Company warned that despite a resolution to the crown crisis the other problems had not disappeared. "Now it really boils down to the restructuring story and the fundamentals in individual companies," he said.
